Definition: from G1487, G1161, and G3361 (sometimes with G1065 added); but if not:--(or) else, if (not, otherwise), otherwise.
BiblicalUsage: This is a phrase, not a single word, built from if and but and not, and it means otherwise or but if not. Jesus warns that if you do your alms before men to be seen, otherwise you have no reward of your Father, and He tells His disciples that in His Father's house are many mansions, and if it were not so He would have told them. The phrase turns on a condition, and the warning or the comfort follows from it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus uses otherwise to make the stakes plain, because the condition decides whether the reward stands or falls.
RelatedTopics: Fear of the Lord; Faith; Hope
